title: A Wide Dynamic Range Differential Drive CMOS Rectifier for μWatts RF Energy Harvesting Systems
problem: RF energy harvesting systems require rectifiers that maintain high power conversion efficiency (PCE) across a wide range of input power levels while minimizing reverse conduction losses.
motivation: Wide dynamic range RF rectifiers are essential for practical IoT and wearable applications where input RF power varies significantly. Conventional rectifiers suffer from efficiency degradation at low input powers due to reverse conduction losses.
method: Self-biased differential drive rectifier topology in 65-nm CMOS technology. The design minimizes reverse conduction losses through optimized biasing while maintaining low forward conduction losses.
key_novelty: Novel self-bias scheme that achieves 14 dB dynamic range with 60.5% peak PCE—74% improvement in DR compared to cross-coupled rectifiers.
contributions: Wide dynamic range rectifier design with self-biasing mechanism
Demonstrated 60.5% peak PCE at -28.9 dBm input power at 953 MHz
74% improvement in dynamic range over conventional cross-coupled designs
limitations: Evaluation limited to simulation; silicon results not reported. Performance metrics at single frequency (953 MHz) and fixed load impedance.
primary_theme: Analog low-power circuits for RF energy harvesting
